newsitem.title: JAPAN: Indonesia petrochemical firm to up output - Marubeni.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia petrochemical firm to up output - Marubeni.

text.p: Indonesian petrochemical firm PT Chandra Asri plans to invest $500-$600 million to boost petrochemical product output at a plant in West Java, joint venture partner Marubeni Corp said on Friday.

The petrochemical complex in Cilegon will increase output of ethylene by 160,000 tonnes to an annual 670,000 tonnes, propylene by 60,000 tonnes to 300,000 tonnes and polyethylene by 200,000 tonnes to 500,000 tonnes, a Marubeni spokesman said.
New facilities to produce 180,000 tonnes of polypropylene will also be built, he said.
Chandra Asri is partly owned by President Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo and timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu.
Marubeni and Showa Denko KK share a combined 25 percent interest in the firm.
